metadata.name: Houndkeeper
metadata.description: Components and boundaries of Houndkeeper: a Go2 Air carrying a Maker Arm, running on DimOS, that keeps a house floor clear at night. Components without a source-path live outside this repository (in the DimOS fork, on the robot, or as hardware), or are planned and have no code yet.
metadata.observed: 2026-09-24; DimOS fork at a7492431f (upstream main 6043c7371), MuJoCo 3.10.0

nodes.name: House network
nodes.description: The trust boundary. Everything seen in the house (camera frames, recordings, photos, demonstrations, datasets) stays on machines inside it. The robot's segment cannot reach the internet. What may cross outward: geometry, telemetry, logs, metrics, code, text with no house data, and footage deliberately chosen for publication.

nodes.name: Internet
nodes.description: Outside the house. Reached only from the development machines, for code, model downloads, upstream pull requests and text-only hosted models.

nodes.name: Unitree Go2 Air
nodes.description: The robot base: legs, head lidar and camera, battery, Unitree's own walking controller. Firmware pinned; no update taken unplanned.

nodes.name: Maker Arm
nodes.description: MakerMods 6-joint arm with a parallel gripper and wrist camera, mounted on the robot's back at the position given by robot-parameters. RobStride RS02 motors on joints 2-3, RS00 elsewhere.

nodes.name: Jaw pads
nodes.description: TPU pads that slip over the Maker Arm's two fingertips, generated from the finger's CAD with a shared printability check; the same shape is the pads' collision model in the sims.

nodes.name: Leader arm
nodes.description: MakerMods leader arm for teleoperating the Maker Arm to record demonstrations.

nodes.name: Development laptop
nodes.description: RTX 2070 laptop: runs the sims, the local VLM and training. All compute is local; no cloud GPUs.

nodes.name: R720 server
nodes.description: House server: long sim runs and storage of recordings and datasets.

nodes.name: DimOS
nodes.description: Dimensional's robot OS, used through this project's fork (github.com/dimensionalOS/dimos). Capabilities are DimOS modules and skills; changes that belong in DimOS go upstream.

nodes.name: DimOS navigation and mapping
nodes.description: DimOS's mapping, localisation, costmap and navigation for the base. Upstream code, used unchanged except for patches kept as files in this repository.

nodes.name: DimOS streams
nodes.description: DimOS's typed streams between modules: camera images, lidar, odometry, commands.

nodes.name: DimOS arm interface
nodes.description: DimOS's manipulator adapter protocol and registry (dimos/hardware/manipulators). Every arm DimOS drives is an adapter listed in the registry and implementing this protocol.

interfaces.description: The ManipulatorAdapter protocol, as of the fork at a7492431f: connect and disconnect; activate and deactivate; info, DOF and joint limits; control mode; read joint positions, velocities and efforts (gripper as the last joint entry, in the adapter's own gripper unit); write joint positions and velocities; stop; enable and read enabled; read error and clear errors; optional Cartesian position and force-torque.

nodes.name: Maker Arm adapter
nodes.description: Planned. The Maker Arm as a DimOS manipulator adapter, in the DimOS fork, offered upstream. Talks to the arm through MakerMods' maker-arm-sdk. The same adapter code drives the simulated arm.

interfaces.description: Read joint positions of all six joints and the gripper.
Write joint position targets for the six joints.
Open and close the gripper, as the last joint entry of positions and commands.
Enable and disable the motors, and read whether they are enabled.

nodes.name: DimOS MuJoCo sim
nodes.description: DimOS's simulator: a MuJoCo process standing in for the robot, publishing the same streams as the real robot. Its Go2 is a Go1 body and walking policy (see the Go1 stand-in waymark).

interfaces.description: The robot's clock (dimos.utils.clock, a fork addition offered upstream): the sim publishes a clock that advances with sim time (DIMOS_SIM_CLOCK), holds every injected delay on it and stamps every message on it; modules on the robot's side read time through clock.now, sleep and wait, which are the wall clock on the real robot.

nodes.name: Legged manipulator sim
nodes.description: Planned. An extension of DimOS's MuJoCo sim, in the DimOS fork and offered upstream: a walking robot carrying an arm. The dog's walking controller sees only its own legs; posture commands (stand, crouch, lie) switch it to a posture controller.

interfaces.description: The simulated arm's joints and gripper, exposed as a manipulator adapter through dimos-arm-interface.
The simulated wrist camera, published as a DimOS camera stream like the head camera.

nodes.name: Floor overlay module
nodes.description: Houndkeeper's DimOS module that projects head-camera frames onto the floor and compares tonight's floor picture with the stored one to flag what is new.

nodes.name: Look-closer skill
nodes.description: Planned DimOS skill: at a stop, uses the wrist camera to re-locate a find, measure its grip width and direction, and have the local VLM name it. Prototyped in standalone-arm-sim.

nodes.name: Pick skill
nodes.description: Planned DimOS skill: grasp, lift, carry to the bin on the back, stow. Scripted grasp first; a trained policy through dimos-policy-runner when it scores better. Prototyped in standalone-arm-sim.

nodes.name: Grasp proposers
nodes.description: Behind one interface, the pick's choice of grasp: from the look-closer's result (its looks, item masks, stereo heights, camera poses) to grasps best first in DimOS's grasp message (GraspCandidateArray), with each grasp's grip width and how far the pick may adapt it. Houndkeeper's own proposer (the default) works from the look as it is; DimOS's point-cloud proposers (HeuristicGraspModule, GraspGenX) through an adapter that builds the cloud from the look. Chosen by configuration.

nodes.name: DimOS grasp generators
nodes.description: Upstream DimOS modules implementing its GraspGenSpec (an object's point cloud in, scored grasp poses out): HeuristicGraspModule, and GraspGenX in its own isolated environment.

nodes.name: Local VLM
nodes.description: A small vision-language model (Moondream, through DimOS's wrapper) running on the development laptop's GPU. It only ever sees one wrist-camera crop and never leaves the house network.

nodes.name: DimOS recorder and dataset tools
nodes.description: DimOS's recording format and its demonstration recorder and dataset preparation (to LeRobot datasets).

nodes.name: DimOS policy runner
nodes.description: DimOS's module that runs a trained LeRobot policy on the robot.

nodes.name: Robot parameters
nodes.description: The one place a physical number lives, each labelled vendor, measured, sim, estimate or unknown with its source. Read through houndkeeper.params.get('group.name'); an unknown value raises rather than being guessed. Also where the workspace is: the sibling checkouts beside this repository (houndkeeper.workspace).

interfaces.description: get('group.name') returns the value; raises when the value is unknown.

nodes.name: Standalone arm sims
nodes.description: Fast MuJoCo test loops outside DimOS for single controls: the Go1 stand-in with the Maker Arm, postures, grasp, tip, walk, reach, power and mount scenarios, and the standalone vertical slice. Viewer on by default.

nodes.name: House nights sim
nodes.description: Many simulated nights in one house on DimOS's sim, with changing litter, stains and furniture, scoring the floor comparison.

nodes.name: Sim harness
nodes.description: Runs a named scenario with one command, opens the viewer unless told not to, and appends the result with the code version to the results history.

nodes.name: Training pipeline
nodes.description: Planned. Records demonstrations (scripted sim grasps, leader-arm teleoperation), builds datasets and trains picking policies on the development laptop. Data stays in the house.

nodes.name: Real data replay and calibration
nodes.description: Runs recordings through the perception code, and holds the procedures that measure robot parameters on the real hardware.

nodes.name: CAD reference export
nodes.description: Exports the Go2 and the Maker Arm, and the arm on the robot at the mount position from robot-parameters, as millimetre STL files for designing the printed mount; caches Unitree's own Go2 CAD (STEP) as light meshes and a hole index, kept out of git.

nodes.name: Printed mount
nodes.description: The parametric parts that put the arm, its host and the bin on the robot's back (adapter, removable module, bench plate, bin, hat seat), generated in build123d from robot-parameters and the reference models, with their print files, load cases for the finite-element analysis, and the mass, stiffness, magnet and clearance estimates.

nodes.name: Project map
nodes.description: Makes the project map with the Railyard Method's map command, notes named as dated, and checks the page for addresses and anything from real/.env or real/local/ before it is kept.

nodes.name: Hosted text model
nodes.description: Optional. A hosted language model used for text that carries no house data. Never sent images or recordings.

nodes.name: On-robot arm computer
nodes.description: In work (2 Oct 2026). First hardware: a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B (already on hand): 1 GB RAM, hardware H.264 encoder, 2.4 GHz-only Wi-Fi. Upgrade path if it falls short: a Raspberry Pi 4 with 2 GB (list price $55 since February 2026, per Raspberry Pi's price announcements; 4 GB and up rose far more). A small computer riding on the robot, powered from the Air's pack through a 5 V buck converter. It is the Maker Arm's CAN host (USB CAN adapter; the SDK drives the arm over CAN) and runs the Maker Arm adapter locally so a lost network link stops the arm on the spot. It captures the wrist camera and streams it over the house Wi-Fi to the development laptop, where the heavy models run. Needed because the Go2 Air has no user compute and the arm and camera are USB devices that must be within cable reach. Before the arm arrives it is also the robot's voice, ears and eyes: a Bluetooth speaker, a USB microphone and WS2812 eye lights (the Go2 Air has no speaker or microphone).

nodes.name: Wrist camera
nodes.description: USB camera on the Maker Arm's wrist bracket. Placement may change after a camera-placement sweep in sim.

nodes.name: Tidy module
nodes.description: Houndkeeper's DimOS module (houndkeeper.tidy) that runs the tidy loop: finds items with the head camera, parks beside each with DimOS navigation, lies down through the Go2 connection's postures, looks closer and picks through the shared pick routine, driving the arm through DimOS's arm interface and a kinematic copy of the robot, every arm and posture command through one arm guard (still, down, inside the tip-safety envelope). Provides the look-closer and pick skills. Keeps to the operating area: stores it with the map, publishes it to DimOS's costmap layer as keep-out zones and virtual walls, and serves the cockpit's Area page.

nodes.name: Houndkeeper on DimOS's sim
nodes.description: The model hook DimOS's sim calls to mount the Maker Arm (the same definition the standalone sims use) and place library items, the environment it needs, and the run and scoring scripts for tidy runs on DimOS. It also renders the robot's head and wrist cameras through Filament (mujofil, rebuilt for DimOS's MuJoCo), for DimOS's sim and the standalone arm sims.

nodes.name: Robot segment
nodes.description: Inside the house network: the robot, the arm host and the laptop on a small router with no upstream (dog-first-boot [MTv], decision [ZaY]). No route to the internet; the laptop joins by cable and never forwards to its own internet link.

nodes.name: Phone cockpit
nodes.description: DimOS's Cockpit laid out for a phone (phone-cockpit [Swt]): video and touch driving with the deadman stop, and houndkeeper's own Procedures and Status pages as Cockpit extensions loaded from the relay's --extensions-dir. The robot-side CockpitData module runs the calibration procedures live and publishes the robot's status; the relay runs on the laptop, reached over Tailscale. The butler's morning log (morning-log [uoW]) is written from a finished night's own outputs into the night's directory, its crops only from recordings the catalog clears.

nodes.name: Project service
nodes.description: The project on the phone (project-app [C3p]): an always-on houndkeeper blueprint on the laptop that registers with the cockpit relay as the participant "project", beside the robot, and carries only the project's pages (Last night [RzM]; Marks and Review, a real night scored from the phone, sim-to-real [oWO]; Cockpit extensions in cockpit/extensions/), so they work with no robot or sim running ([eTc]). Last night is read only; the scoring pages write only marks and judgements beside the real night, logged. Its launcher binds the relay only to loopback or the laptop's Tailscale address ([Dlx]).
